key_insight: ENGINE bridges the variance–information trade-off in zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning by using high-dimensional probes to correct low-dimensional updates.
engineering_relevance: It adapts variational multiscale ideas from computational mechanics to improve memory-efficient LLM optimization.
method: Treat low- and high-dimensional parameter spaces as coarse and fine scales.
Alternate between scales through a multigrid-style V-cycle.
Inject fine-scale information to correct coarse-scale sampling.
evidence_signal: On standard LLM benchmarks, ENGINE reports higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing zeroth-order methods, with up to 2.61× speed-up in forward passes and no additional peak memory overhead.
watch_item: Theoretical guarantees depend on assumptions, and the abstract does not specify how gains vary across models, tasks, or probing schedules.
paper_title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
